chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Talib 'Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:

Concerning a mouse that falls into a well, then a man performs wudu (ablution) from it and offers salat (prayer) while he does not know: should he repeat the salat (prayer) and wash his garment? He said: “He does not repeat the salat (prayer), nor does he wash his garment.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which the water was taken
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse; the source of possible najasah mentioned in the case
key_terms.ثَوْبَهُ: his garment, regarding whether it must be washed
key_terms.فَيَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution) using that water
key_terms.لَا يَعْلَمُ: he does not know; indicating ignorance of the impurity at the time
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: he repeats; referring to whether the salat (prayer) must be performed again

ai.seo_question: If a mouse falls into a well and someone unknowingly uses its water for wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer), must he repeat the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who used water from a well into which a mouse had fallen, without knowing it, and then performed salat (prayer). The ruling states that he does not need to repeat the salat (prayer) or wash his garment, indicating the legal effect of ignorance in this case.
